OSPS-AC-01.01.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and allows only secure second factors (TOTP, security keys/passkeys, GitHub Mobile; no SMS), so no account can read or change a repository's sensitive settings without MFA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

OSPS-AC-02.01.justification: The organization's base permission is read, so a new member or collaborator gets read access until an owner grants more. The only elevated grants on this repository are the three owners' admin. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-AC-03.01.justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main. Its one bypass actor holds it in pull_request mode, which never allows a direct push. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-03.02.justification: The main-integrity ruleset forbids deleting main and has no bypass actor. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-04.01.justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at the organization and the repository, and cannot approve pull requests. Every workflow also sets permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning

OSPS-AC-04.02.justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top, and a job adds only the scopes it uses. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does

OSPS-BR-01.01.justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run. Event fields and inputs reach run: steps only through env:, and zizmor's template-injection audit in the required lint check refuses the unsafe form. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

OSPS-BR-01.03.justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request and pull_request_review_comment triggers, which give a fork no secrets and a read-only token. The review job, which holds a secret, runs only when the head repository is this one. On issue_comment, the mention job, which holds a secret on any pull request, checks out the default branch. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml

OSPS-BR-01.04.justification: The only workflow_dispatch input is mutation.yml's profile, a choice from a fixed list. A release tag's name is checked against the package version before anything is built. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/mutation.yml

OSPS-BR-02.01.justification: Each release has a unique calendar version, YYYY.M.D, set by a signed v* tag. release.yml refuses a tag that differs from the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases

OSPS-BR-02.02.justification: Every release asset carries the version in its file name: the sdist, the wheel, the CycloneDX SBOM and the attestation bundle. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases/latest

OSPS-BR-03.01.justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://btclib.readthedocs.io/.

OSPS-BR-03.02.justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS only. PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle. https://pypi.org/project/btclib/

OSPS-BR-04.01.justification: Every release has a CHANGELOG.md entry, listing every change, and a RELEASE_NOTES.md entry, listing what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included. The GitHub release body is the release notes. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

OSPS-BR-05.01.justification: Pipelines install dependencies with uv: from the committed uv.lock with --locked, except the jobs that test a fresh resolution and the build backend, which uv build takes within pyproject.toml's uv_build range. The post-release install check uses uv pip install. Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#uvlock

OSPS-BR-06.01.justification: Every PyPI file from 2026.8.7 on carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing. Every GitHub release from v2026.8.21 on carries a Sigstore provenance bundle covering each asset's SHA-256. Release tags are signed from v2026.8.21 on. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases/latest

OSPS-BR-07.01.justification: Secret scanning and push protection are on, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused. The detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.secrets.baseline

OSPS-BR-07.02.justification: A secret is an environment secret only the owners reach, and any other store's entry is recorded in the spending repository's REPOSITORY.md. A secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected, and the list is reviewed yearly. btclib-org/.github's tests/secrets_test.py refuses an unrecorded entry. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2913-L2940

OSPS-DO-01.01.justification: The user guide, docs/source/guide.rst, and the API reference are published at https://btclib.readthedocs.io/. tests/docs_examples_test.py runs the guide's examples.

OSPS-DO-02.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report form asks for what a report needs. SECURITY.md sends a vulnerability to a private channel instead. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml

OSPS-DO-03.01.justification: SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command for the release assets, and RELEASING.md the check that rebuilds the sdist from its tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-03.02.justification: The verify command pins the signer: --repo names this repository and --signer-workflow the workflow that signed, so an attestation from any other repository or workflow is refused. SECURITY.md names the signer of each release. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-04.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-05.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, so a release stops receiving security updates when the next one is published. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-06.01.justification: pyproject.toml states why each runtime dependency is there. Dependencies come from PyPI through uv, are pinned in uv.lock, and are updated by weekly grouped Dependabot pull requests with a seven-day cooldown. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#dependabot-and-pre-commitci

OSPS-DO-07.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock, and uv build makes the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-01.01.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's *Roles* names who holds access to sensitive resources: the maintainer, the only bypass actor, and the three owners, each an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-01.02.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's *Roles* describes the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-02.01.justification: Proposed changes and usage questions are discussed publicly in the repository's issues, which have a question form, and pull requests. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/issues

OSPS-GV-03.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: an issue first, one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-03.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a contribution must meet: one subject, a Signed-off-by trailer on every commit, the gates CI runs, 100% line and branch coverage, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-04.01.justification: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/GOVERNANCE.md#L44-L46 : a grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there.

OSPS-LE-01.01.justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, so a pull request cannot merge unless every commit carries its author's Signed-off-by: trailer. Web commits are signed off automatically. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

OSPS-LE-02.01.justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-02.02.justification: The released wheels and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/btclib/

OSPS-LE-03.01.justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-03.02.justification: The LICENSE file ships in every release asset: at the sdist root and in the wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. https://pypi.org/project/btclib/#files

OSPS-QA-01.01.justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib

OSPS-QA-01.02.justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature. main refuses force-pushes and requires linear history. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/commits/main

OSPS-QA-02.01.justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies ([project] dependencies, optional extras and dependency groups), and the committed uv.lock resolves and pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-02.02.justification: The release is pure Python. Every release from v2026.8.21 on attaches a CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM, generated from the built wheel and covered by the release attestation. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases/latest

OSPS-QA-03.01.justification: main requires the six CI status checks, up to date with main (strict). enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge without them is a manual bypass, which the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-QA-04.01.justification: The organization standard's *Which repositories, and how far* lists every btclib-org repository and its tier. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far

OSPS-QA-04.02.justification: Each release is built from this repository alone. The sibling packages it depends on are released from their own repositories. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib

OSPS-QA-05.01.justification: No generated executable is committed. The binary files are Bitcoin-serialized data (blocks, transactions, scripts, P2P messages) used as test data and fuzz seeds, and the Sphinx inventory python.inv. The lint gate's check-added-large-files keeps build output out. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib

OSPS-QA-05.02.justification: The binary files are Bitcoin-serialized data (blocks, transactions, scripts, P2P messages) used as test data and fuzz seeds, which the library itself decodes, and the Sphinx inventory python.inv. tests/_data/README.md pins each vendored test file to its source, and docs/source/conf.py gives the command that fetches the inventory. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/tests/_data/README.md

OSPS-QA-06.01.justification: test.yml runs the test suite on every pull request, and its aggregate check, 'test: every job passed', is required on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

OSPS-QA-06.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the tests and says which workflows run them and which gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-QA-06.03.justification: The policy is 100% line and branch coverage (CONTRIBUTING.md; standard section 8). pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100, so untested new code fails the required test check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-07.01.justification: The maintainer is the ruleset's bypass actor and merges his own pull requests without another person's approval, so main does not require a non-author approval. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#review

OSPS-SA-01.01.justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents the components, their layers and where the software reaches outside the process. ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Trust boundaries* and *Threat model* name the actors and what each can do. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md

OSPS-SA-02.01.justification: The API reference at https://btclib.readthedocs.io/ is generated from the docstrings of every public module, and a docs test fails when a shipped module is missing from it. CONTRIBUTING.md's *The public surface* states what is public.

OSPS-SA-03.01.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: claims, threat model, trust boundaries and how each common weakness is countered. SECURITY.md's *Limitations, not vulnerabilities* records the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-SA-03.02.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names the assets, the adversaries and what is not defended. Its *Trust boundaries* maps where untrusted input enters. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-VM-01.01.justification: SECURITY.md gives the private reporting channels and states the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L19

OSPS-VM-02.01.justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org, which reaches the three organization owners. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-VM-03.01.justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/security/advisories/new

OSPS-VM-04.01.justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on this repository, as SECURITY.md commits to. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/security/advisories

OSPS-VM-04.02.justification: Each release's CycloneDX SBOM lists in its vulnerabilities array every vulnerability judged not to affect it, with the reason, from the tree's .github/vex.toml. None is judged so today, so the tree has no such file. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L3120-L3135

OSPS-VM-05.01.justification: Every pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action, which fails on an added or changed dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2892-L2909

OSPS-VM-05.02.justification: release.yml runs uv audit over every dependency the wheel declares before any publish job. An advisory, or a service it cannot reach, stops the release. The only exemption is an id the release's own signed VEX states as not affecting it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L3149-L3160

OSPS-VM-05.03.justification: Every pull request runs the Dependency review job, and "lint / Dependency review" is a required check on main, so a pull request that breaks the policy cannot merge. Policy: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2892-L2909

OSPS-VM-06.01.justification: The standard's section 5 sets the threshold at zero: ruff runs select = ALL, bandit's S rules included, and each finding is fixed or suppressed in place with a reason. zizmor holds workflows to the same. CodeQL alerts have no stated threshold. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff

OSPS-VM-06.02.justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request (ruff with the S rules, strict mypy, zizmor, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding not suppressed in place with a reason. CodeQL also runs on every pull request but is not a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml

access_continuity.justification: The organization has three owners, fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, each an admin of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments. If one becomes unavailable, the other two can still close issues, merge changes and release. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity

accessibility_best_practices.justification: btclib is a library with no user interface, so accessibility practices have no surface to apply to. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md

assurance_case.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md states the threat model, the trust boundaries, the secure-design argument and the argument against common implementation weaknesses this criterion asks for. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

automated_integration_testing.justification: test.yml runs the suite, and integration-bitcoind.yml runs tests/integration against Bitcoin Core on regtest, on every pull request and push to main. Both are required checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

build_non_recursive.justification: This tree builds no native binaries, so there is no recursive-build question to answer. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_preserve_debug.justification: No native build or installation step exists to strip or preserve debugging information. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_repeatable.justification: btclib is pure Python built with uv_build, with no compilation step. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_reproducible.justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit. sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds a release from its signed tag and verifies it against the release's PyPI attestation, and RELEASING.md tells a user how to do the same. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml

build_standard_variables.justification: btclib is pure Python built with uv_build, so no compiler or linker runs for CC, CFLAGS or LDFLAGS to reach. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

bus_factor.justification: Only the maintainer has deep knowledge of the code: in the last 12 months every other person made three commits or fewer. The three organization owners hold admin access, and one of them did the security review in issue #2450. The project does not claim a second knowledgeable maintainer.

code_of_conduct.justification: btclib-org/.github's CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is this repository's code of conduct, through GitHub's organization-wide default; the community-profile API reports it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

code_review_standards.justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/REVIEWING.md

coding_standards.justification: pyproject.toml's [tool.ruff] selects every rule (select = ["ALL"]) with a documented ignore list, and [tool.mypy] runs in strict mode. CONTRIBUTING.md names both and the commands that run them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

coding_standards_enforced.justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run in .pre-commit-config.yaml, which the required lint check runs on every pull request. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

contribution_requirements.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the coding-standard, lint-gate and 100%-coverage requirements a contribution must meet before it can land. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

contributors_unassociated.justification: Only one contributor is significant: in the last 12 months the maintainer made more than 1600 commits and every other person three or fewer.

copyright_per_file.justification: Every Python file opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/src/btclib/__init__.py

crypto_algorithm_agility.justification: btclib implements the Bitcoin protocol, whose consensus rules fix secp256k1, SHA-256 and the signature schemes; another algorithm needs a soft fork first, and the project follows one when it activates. The curve and hash agility is in btclib-ecc, which btclib depends on. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md

crypto_call.justification: btclib calls libraries for its primitives: curve arithmetic and signature schemes from btclib-ecc, BIP324's ChaCha20 and ChaCha20-Poly1305 from cryptography, hashes from hashlib. It writes only what Bitcoin's specifications build on them (MuHash3072, the BIP324 key schedule). Its RIPEMD-160 is Bitcoin Core's own Python copy, used only where hashlib has none. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/tree/main/src/btclib

crypto_certificate_verification.justification: btclib performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst

crypto_credential_agility.justification: btclib has no configuration file or credential store: a private key or password is a function argument, never read from or written to a file. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

crypto_keylength.justification: The keys btclib works with are secp256k1 keys, about 128 bits of security, above NIST's 112-bit floor for 2030; BIP324's ciphers use 256-bit keys. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

crypto_pfs.justification: btclib.p2p.bip324 implements BIP324's key schedule: the session keys come from an ElligatorSwift ECDH over the key pair BIP324 makes fresh for each connection, and both ciphers rekey every 224 packets. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/src/btclib/p2p/bip324.py

crypto_published.justification: btclib imports its curve arithmetic from btclib_ecc, which calls btclib-secp256k1 (bindings to Bitcoin Core's libsecp256k1) wherever a call can use them and otherwise runs Python arithmetic; SECURITY.md states when each applies and `btclib_ecc.curves.is_libsecp256k1_serving()` tells a caller which. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

crypto_random.justification: btclib draws randomness only from Python's `secrets` module (the BMS nonce, the transaction input and output shuffle); ECDSA nonces are deterministic (RFC 6979). Key, mnemonic and nonce generation is in btclib_ecc and btclib-wallet, which hold their own entries. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/tree/main/src/btclib

crypto_tls12.justification: btclib performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst

crypto_used_network.justification: btclib does not communicate over a network, as docs/source/guide.rst states. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst

crypto_verification_private.justification: btclib performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst

crypto_weaknesses.justification: btclib's only SHA-1 is Bitcoin script's OP_SHA1, which the protocol requires and which runs with usedforsecurity=False. The curve schemes and ECIES are btclib_ecc's. SECURITY.md documents where a secret reaches the Python fallback. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

dco.justification: Every commit carries its author's Signed-off-by: trailer: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a pull request with a commit lacking it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

dependency_monitoring.justification: Dependabot version updates are configured in .github/dependabot.yml, and Dependabot security updates are enabled on the repository. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml

discussion.justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.

documentation_achievements.justification: README.md shows the OpenSSF Best Practices badge, linked to this project's page. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md

documentation_architecture.justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents the module layout and layer boundaries of this tree's software. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md

documentation_basics.justification: Some documentation basics file contents found.

documentation_current.justification: docs.yml builds the docs with -W -n on every pull request, and the build is a required check. The API reference is generated from the shipped docstrings. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml

documentation_quick_start.justification: docs/source/guide.rst is a task-oriented quick start, and tests/docs_examples_test.py runs its examples, so a stale example fails the suite. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/docs/source/guide.rst

documentation_roadmap.justification: The organization's ROADMAP.md covers the period until 2027-09-30, is reviewed every September, and states what is intended and what is not. This tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md

documentation_security.justification: SECURITY.md's *Limitations, not vulnerabilities* states what a user can and cannot expect: constant-time behaviour, key zeroization, and which operations use libsecp256k1 and which the Python fallback. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions.justification: The suite runs under pytest, which rewrites `assert` statements, and the fuzz and mutation jobs run the library with assertions enabled (no `-O`). https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

dynamic_analysis_unsafe.justification: This tree ships pure Python, a memory-safe language; it produces no software written in a memory-unsafe language for a dynamic memory-safety tool to run against. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

external_dependencies.justification: Every dependency is declared in machine-readable form in pyproject.toml's [project.dependencies] and dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

floss_license.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

floss_license_osi.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

governance.justification: The organization's GOVERNANCE.md documents how decisions are made, the maintainer's bypass and every role. This tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md

hardened_site.justification: https://btclib.org/btclib/ sends Content-Security-Policy (with frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Strict-Transport-Security. Check with curl -sI https://btclib.org/btclib/

hardening.justification: ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit S rules, so unsafe deserialization, weak temp files and shell injection fail the lint gate. CodeQL also runs on every pull request, every push to main and weekly. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

implement_secure_design.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles* argues how each principle applies to ARCHITECTURE.md's layers. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

input_validation.justification: Every public function validates its inputs and refuses what is invalid; the unchecked work lives in a private twin the public function calls once it has validated, as CONTRIBUTING.md requires. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

installation_common.justification: btclib is on PyPI, so pip install and pip uninstall install and remove it. README.md gives the command. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md

installation_development_quick.justification: uv sync installs the whole development environment in one command. CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

installation_standard_variables.justification: Installation is pip install, which follows pip's own install-location conventions; the project has no installer of its own. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

interfaces_current.justification: ruff's UP and FA rules flag deprecated standard-library and typing constructs. pytest runs with filterwarnings = ["error"], so a deprecation warning fails the suite, and deps-latest.yml runs it weekly against each dependency's newest release. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

internationalization.justification: btclib produces no end-user text to localize; its output is hex, addresses and error messages for developers. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/README.md

know_common_errors.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md argues how each common implementation weakness (CWE-20, 209, 248, 330/338, 347, 502, 755, 843 and others) is countered in this tree. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

know_secure_design.justification: The primary developer wrote the assurance case, which argues each secure-design principle against the architecture. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

license_location.justification: Non-trivial license location file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/LICENSE>.

license_per_file.justification: Every Python file states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/src/btclib/__init__.py

maintenance_or_update.justification: Only the latest release is supported (SECURITY.md). For upgrading, RELEASING.md runs griffe check against the previous tag, and RELEASE_NOTES.md lists each breaking change with its before and after. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

regression_tests_added50.justification: Every bug fix to src/ merged in the last six months also changes tests/. The 100% line and branch coverage gate also fails a fix whose new code no test runs. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged

release_notes.justification: Non-trivial release notes file in repository: <https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md>.

release_notes_vulns.justification: The release notes name each advisory a release fixes by its GHSA id; for example, v2026.10.8 names GHSA-c6h8-5hv5-3gv7. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

repo_distributed.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.

repo_interim.justification: development is on the main branch of https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib

repo_public.justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.

repo_track.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.

report_process.justification: SECURITY.md gives the private reporting process. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

report_tracker.justification: Issues are tracked in this repository's GitHub Issues, with issue forms; cross-repository issues go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/issues

require_2FA.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member. https://github.com/btclib-org

roles_responsibilities.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's *Roles* describes the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

secure_2FA.justification: The btclib-org GitHub organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and has 'Only allow secure two-factor methods' selected, which refuses SMS as a second factor: only TOTP apps, security keys/passkeys and GitHub Mobile are accepted. Read from the organization's security settings on 2026-09-30 and recorded at https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

security_review.justification: pmazzocchi, an owner other than the maintainer, did a security review on 2026-09-30: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/issues/2450 . It is pinned to a commit, checks every claim and trust boundary of ASSURANCE_CASE.md, states what it did not cover, and files each finding as an issue.

signed_releases.justification: Every PyPI file from 2026.8.7 on carries a PEP 740 attestation, and every GitHub release from v2026.8.21 on a Sigstore provenance bundle. Release tags are signed from v2026.8.21 on. SECURITY.md gives the verify command. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/releases/latest

sites_password_security.justification: The project sites (GitHub, PyPI, Read the Docs, btclib.org) store no passwords of this project's; authentication is theirs. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

small_tasks.justification: Small tasks for newcomers carry the label "good first issue", which CONTRIBUTING.md sets aside for a first contribution. 27 such issues were open at some time in the last 12 months. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/issues?q=label%3A%22good+first+issue%22

static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities.justification: CodeQL runs on every pull request, every push to main and weekly, and ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit S rules. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

test.justification: test.yml runs the pytest suite, gated at 100% line and branch coverage, on every pull request. It checks vectors from the BIPs, Bitcoin Core and Core's qa-assets, and tests/_data/README.md pins each vendored file to its upstream commit. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/actions/workflows/test.yml

test_branch_coverage80.justification: Branch coverage is measured (`branch = true` under `[tool.coverage.run]`) and the 100% gate includes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_continuous_integration.justification: test.yml runs the suite on every pull request and push to main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/actions/workflows/test.yml

test_policy_mandated.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires 100% coverage, and fail_under = 100.0 fails the required check for any new code without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

test_statement_coverage80.justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0 under [tool.coverage.report], gated on every pull request. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_statement_coverage90.justification: Coverage is gated at 100% (`fail_under = 100.0` under `[tool.coverage.report]`) on every pull request. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

tests_documented_added.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the 100% coverage requirement, so new functionality needs a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

two_person_review.justification: The maintainer is the ruleset's bypass actor and merges his own pull requests without another person's approval, so main does not require a non-author approval. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#review

updateable_reused_components.justification: Reused components are standard-library modules or PyPI packages pinned in uv.lock. Dependabot updates them weekly through pull requests that run the full suite. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml

version_semver.justification: Versions are calendar versions, YYYY.M.D, and each release is tagged v<version>. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github#12-releasing

version_tags_signed.justification: Release tags are signed from v2026.8.21 on, and GitHub verifies each. RELEASING.md signs each tag with git tag -s and reads the signature back after the push. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/tags

vulnerability_report_credit.justification: The reporter of GHSA-9fr5-46w5-5f9r, pmazzocchi, is credited as finder on the advisory. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/security/advisories/GHSA-9fr5-46w5-5f9r

vulnerability_report_response.justification: The one vulnerability reported by someone other than the maintainer in the last six months, GHSA-9fr5-46w5-5f9r, was opened on 2026-09-30 and fixed and published on 2026-10-03. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/security/advisories/GHSA-9fr5-46w5-5f9r

vulnerability_response_process.justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels (a GitHub security advisory, or security at btclib dot org), who sees a report, and how to request a CVE. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/SECURITY.md

warnings.justification: ruff runs with select = ["ALL"], mypy with strict = true and pytest with filterwarnings = ["error"], each in a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_fixed.justification: Warnings are not tolerated: ruff, strict mypy and pytest's filterwarnings = ["error"] fail the required checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_strict.justification: ruff runs with select = ["ALL"] and mypy with strict = true, both with zero findings allowed in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib/blob/main/pyproject.toml
